newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nobel laureate's publisher swamped at book fair.
newsitem.headline: Nobel laureate's publisher swamped at book fair.

text.p: The German publisher of Nobel prize-winning poet Wislawa Szymborska said on Thursday it was overjoyed at her award and their stand at the Frankfurt book fair was swamped with well-wishers seeking copies of her books.
"We are overjoyed. She is a great author and we are very proud," said a spokeswoman for the publishing house Suhrkamp which has been translating her works into German since 1973.
"We expect a big boost in sales. She is one of the greatest Polish authors," the spokeswoman said, confirming that the Nobel prize winner was not in Frankfurt.

Seamus Heaney, who last year became Ireland's fourth Nobel winner, was in Frankfurt this week for the opening of the fair, which attracted more than 9,000 publishers from 110 countries. But Heaney's publisher said the poet had left Frankfurt for Krakow, where Szymborska lives, before the prize was announced.
The award surprised observers, who had expected a noveliest to win the $1.12 million award after Heaney won last year.

Jonathan Galassi, president of the Academy of American Poets, said: "This is wonderful news. She is the greatest living author in Poland. It is fabulous. With Seamus Heaney winning last year and now her, it is incredible to have two poets in a row."
